jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Tough Crowd
jokes.joke: At a county fair they put the comedy stage beside the outhouses. I got shoved into the spotlight just as a door behind me opened and a guy staggered out. Before I’d said a word, he yelled, “It’s worse in there.” Tough crowd—I lost a roast battle to a toilet.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Birth Plan
jokes.joke: My sister had a home birth, and the midwife kept saying, 'You're doing amazing, you're the star of this room.' Meanwhile I'm in the corner holding a towel, and suddenly the baby shows up and everyone turns to look at me. I'm like, 'Why's everyone looking at me?' Turns out the towel was the only thing between us and a very rough first impression.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Stage Fright
jokes.joke: People always talk about being thrust into the spotlight like it's some glamorous big break. Last summer at a rustic outdoor wedding, a sudden gust of wind ripped the door clean off the outhouse, exposing me mid-squat to eighty guests right as the bride walked down the aisle. You don't know true panic until you have to decide whether to wipe or take a bow.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Outhouse Delivery
jokes.joke: I hired a midwife who was big on traditional births. She insisted we do it in an outhouse for authenticity. I'm outside holding a flashlight, pacing like a maniac, when she yells, "It's a boy!" Then I hear a splash. She walks out, hands me the baby, and says, "You might want to call a plumber before the next one."

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Accidental Celebrity
jokes.joke: I got my first taste of fame working at Blockbuster. One night the local news came to interview the last customer renting a DVD, and I happened to be standing behind him. The reporter shoved a microphone in my face like I was witnessing history. I wasn't prepared for sudden celebrity, so when they asked for a comment I blurted, "Be kind, rewind," like I was accepting a lifetime achievement award.

scores.comment: Clear first-person setup and correct seed use, but the towel logic is muddy and the payoff does not land cleanly enough for a strong laugh.
Strong visual premise, clean escalation, and a crisp final choice. The exposure angle is somewhat predictable from the ingredients, but the punchline earns the laugh.
The splash-to-plumber turn is clear and usable, but the outhouse-as-traditional-birth premise feels contrived and the final gag is fairly foreseeable.

Strong visual and a good final choice between wiping and taking a bow. The wedding setup runs long and the 'glamorous big break' opener is a bit generic, but the closer carries the laugh.
Absurd premise of an outhouse birth, but the plumber line is a soft ending and the baby-in-toilet beat is more uneasy than funny. The turn is predictable once the splash arrives.
The 'Be kind, rewind' blurt is a recognizable and affectionate payoff, with a solid setup. The final simile over-explains the line, so it slightly dulls the snap.
